sections.html:
Spring Valley is a dense village in Rockland County, about 22 miles north of Manhattan and 5 miles north of the New Jersey line. Most of it lies in the Town of Ramapo, with a small western slice in the Town of Clarkstown. Neighbors include Chestnut Ridge to the south, Airmont and Monsey to the west, Hillcrest to the north and Nanuet to the east.

The village sits next to the New York State Thruway (Interstate 87), and the Spring Valley Transit Center is the terminus of New Jersey Transit's Pascack Valley Line. That access to rail and highway is a selling point for commuters. Downtown revitalization has meant demolishing abandoned buildings on Main Street and putting mixed-use buildings in their place.

Because the village straddles two towns, the town part of your tax bill depends on the side of the line your parcel is on. Your deed, tax bill and the county's property search will show it.

Spring Valley is crowded and rent-heavy. The village has 2.01 square miles of land and 16,442.6 residents per square mile, with 34,482 people as of July 1, 2025, up 4.3% from 2020. Only 25.0% of homes are owner-occupied, and households average 3.63 people.

The population is young and multilingual: 36.0% of residents are under 18 and 75.6% of those age five and up speak a language other than English at home. Marketing in more than one language may reach more of the buyers and tenants here.

With three-quarters of homes rented, a lot of sellers own two-family and multi-family buildings with tenants in place. If yours is one of them, gather leases, rent rolls and any inspection records before you talk to buyers.

The Village of Spring Valley Building Department, at 200 North Main Street, administers the New York State Building Code, Fire Prevention Code, Housing Code and Energy Code along with the village's planning and zoning rules. It issues building permits, certificates of occupancy and water meters, schedules construction inspections and takes complaints. Its inspectors also carry out fire code and housing inspections.

That mix of housing inspections and certificate work makes the department the first call if your house has an unfinished project, an extra apartment or an open complaint. Village Hall answers at (845) 352-1100. The village website links to the Rockland County property search and an interactive county map, which help you confirm lot lines and the correct town.

  • Ask whether every unit in your building has a certificate of occupancy.
  • Ask whether any housing or fire inspection is open.
  • Ask whether the village requires any registration or certificate when a house with tenants changes owners.

A Spring Valley owner usually receives three kinds of tax bill, and they come from different offices. Village taxes are billed and collected by the village itself, and the Town of Ramapo does not collect taxes for the villages. The Village Treasurer's Office at Village Hall takes payments and posts due dates on the bill and in the village's tax portal.

Ramapo's Receiver of Taxes collects the County and Town bill, with the first payment due on or before January 31 and penalties starting in February. School tax penalties start in October. If your bill is over $50 you may pay the County and Town tax in four installments, with a 5% service charge collected by the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance. School taxes arrive on a separate bill.

If you plan to sell, skip the installment plan. It can cause confusion at closing, and the service fee is 5% of the total. At closing you receive credit for the unused portion of the taxes. Under state law an owner stays responsible for taxes even if a bill never arrives, and the town cannot waive statutory penalties.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Rockland County
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded by the Rockland County Clerk at 1 South Main Street in New City. The clerk does not supply deed forms and cannot help prepare one. The deed has to be signed and notarized, include the names and addresses of all sellers and buyers, and carry a Schedule A property description, which you can copy from the current deed of record.

  • Form TP-584 must be signed by all parties, and Form RP-5217 needs at least one grantor and one grantee, with a buyer contact name and a valid phone number.
  • The base recording fee is $45, plus $5 per page, a $6 TP-584 fee and a $10 notification fee.
  • The RP-5217 filing fee is $125 or $250, depending on the property class code and the sale type on the form.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope must come with a mailed submission, or the recorded original is not returned.

The state transfer tax is $2 per $500, or $4 per $1,000 of price. The 1% mansion tax applies only when the taxable consideration is $1 million or more.

sections.h2: What to line up before contract
sections.html:
Start with the parcel: confirm the town, the school district and the village tax account from your bills. Then collect permit records and certificates of occupancy from the Building Department, and ask for the tax status of the village, County and Town, and school bills. A closing attorney can then prepare the deed, Schedule A and transfer forms.

Ramapo's tax office handles school and property taxes for about 30,000 parcels, keeps the tax roll open for public inspection and helps residents, realtors, lenders and title companies who need tax information. A Third Party Request Form is available on its page.

If the building has tenants, add leases, rent ledgers and any inspection notices to the file. Buyers of multi-family buildings in a village where only a quarter of homes are owner-occupied will want to know exactly who lives in each unit and what each pays.

If you would rather not run that gauntlet, a cash buyer can take the building with tenants in place and close on your date, without a lender waiting on inspection notices.

By closing, your attorney should have the signed and notarized deed, the Schedule A description and both transfer forms ready for the Rockland County Clerk in New City. The tax credit for the unused part of the year is worked out at the table, so bring your latest bills from the village, the County and Town, and the school district.

Landlords should also hand over rent ledgers and keys for every unit, and tell tenants in writing who the new owner is. Skipping that step is a common source of confusion after a sale.

faqs.q: Does the Town of Ramapo collect my village taxes?
faqs.a: No. Each village bills and collects its own taxes. In Spring Valley that means the Village Treasurer's Office at 200 North Main Street.

faqs.q: Should I choose installments if I plan to sell?
faqs.a: No. Ramapo's Receiver of Taxes advises against it because of closing confusion and the 5% service fee. At closing you are credited for the unused part of the taxes.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Spring Valley deed?
faqs.a: The Rockland County Clerk in New City records it. The deed must be signed and notarized, and Forms TP-584 and RP-5217 go with it.

faqs.q: What does recording a deed cost in Rockland County?
faqs.a: The base fee is $45, with $5 per page, a $6 TP-584 fee and a $10 notification fee, plus transfer tax and the RP-5217 fee of $125 or $250.

faqs.q: Who inspects houses and issues certificates of occupancy?
faqs.a: The village Building Department at 200 North Main Street. It enforces the state building, fire, housing and energy codes and handles permits and certificates.
